A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MetaSym and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. The complete 18-page v1 and 21-page v2 support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original simulation and prediction results for spring-mesh, open quantum and quadrotor systems, including Table 1 and Figures 2–5.

after.justification: V2 retains the original empirical benchmarks and adds a QuantumLSTM comparison and the experimental analyses in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The symplectic encoder, frozen-encoder decoder training, ControlNet, query/value meta-adaptation and autoregressive inference are retained. V2 clarifies sequence inputs and adds pseudocode normalization consistent with v1's existing mean-MSE objectives; these do not establish a different underlying method.

E1.justification: The three benchmark domains and original datasets remain. Appendix D extends spring-mesh evaluation to transfer from dissipative training to purely conservative systems and to an extreme dissipation/control scenario.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds QuantumLSTM as an evaluated comparator for the quantum task. The existing DHNN, Transformer and MLP comparisons remain unchanged in membership.

E3.justification: New protocols include 3×3 spring-mesh ablations, evaluation across 25 conservative systems, empirical symplectic-defect measurement, and a lower-noise setting for Table 5. Original dataset counts and physical-parameter distributions are retained; newly disclosed benchmark hyperparameters do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds substantial analyses of conservative-system transfer, perturbations under extreme dissipation/control, and the contribution of meta-attention across all three domains. Figure 5's adaptation-loss curves already appeared in v1 and are relocated, rather than newly generated evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions report MSE with standard deviations. The additional results follow the existing reporting practice; neither version supplies new repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: All existing Table 1 entries remain unchanged, but QuantumLSTM adds 244 parameters and MSE 0.891 ± 0.233. Figure 2's spring-mesh error distributions change. Appendix D adds conservative-system MSE 0.050 ± 0.016, symplectic defect 0.999, and six with/without-meta-attention results. These substantially expand the evidence without establishing same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Theorem C.2 and its algebraic proof are retained. V2 explicitly extends the separability assumption to control inputs and removes v1's closing ρ ≪ 1 qualification in favor of an empirical-bound discussion. The new main-text proof sketch largely repeats existing mathematics.

C1.justification: Both versions claim structure-preserving encoding, meta-attentive adaptation, efficient long-horizon prediction and generalization across classical and non-unitary quantum dynamics. The abstract, contributions and conclusion retain these central claims; the added experiments primarily supply supporting evidence.

C2.justification: V2 adds Hessian-based explanations for the different meta-learning choices, interprets the new perturbation and adaptation tests, and attributes benchmark variance to injected noise. It explicitly acknowledges missing real-world validation and softens the earlier specific real-time hardware-threshold assertion to a compactness advantage.

D1.justification: New Appendices E–F disclose A100/RTX 4090 hardware and benchmark-specific optimizers, learning rates, adaptation steps, context windows, dropout, layers, attention heads and stopping epochs. These substantially improve implementation documentation, although Figure 4's 30-step quadrotor context and Table 8's 10-step context remain unreconciled.

R1.justification: V2 adds supporting references on quantum meta-learning, symplectic optimization, Hessians, sequence-window choices and SE(3) representations. The main positioning relative to SympNets, iMODE, DHNNs and Transformers remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The method exposition, benchmark descriptions and figure captions undergo extensive rewriting. Background explanations are shortened, training and inference distinctions are expanded, a proof sketch enters the main text, and limitations and supplementary material receive clearer organization.

P2.justification: V2 changes the main text from two columns to one, redraws Figure 1, and reformats Figures 2–4. It consolidates the six dataset-parameter tables into three paired tables, relocates Figure 5, and adds ablation and hyperparameter tables.

improvement.justification: V2 improves assessability and reproducibility through new component comparisons, physical-regime tests and implementation disclosures missing from v1. These gains are tempered by unreconciled quadrotor context lengths and weaker qualification of the geometric claim: replacing v1's explicit small-ρ caveat with an empirical defect of 0.999 does not establish a uniform small-perturbation guarantee.
